edges.description: Without DHP activity the second step of pyrimidine catabolism stops.
The same enzyme opens the ring of dihydro-5-fluorouracil, so the deficit is also a drug-clearance deficit. Latent until a fluoropyrimidine is given.
Substrates build up and the downstream thymine product is not made.
The accumulating intermediate is excreted, giving dihydropyrimidinuria.
The thymine-derived intermediate is excreted in the same way.
Proposed route to the cognitive phenotype. Not asserted: the intermediates are unknown, and biochemically identical siblings differ in whether they are affected. See the hypothesis of the same name.
Same proposed route. The authors who described the imaging phenotype in the upstream disease state that its mechanism is unknown, which is the same reservation.

The proposed route runs through accumulated 5,6-dihydro-5-fluorouracil, which dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase can convert back to 5-fluorouracil. The intermediate is named in the literature, which is why the edge is INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES rather than direct, but no pharmacokinetic measurement in a DHP-deficient patient was found.
Supplies the substrate the deficient enzyme cannot process. With no administration there is nothing to clear and no toxicity, however low the activity.
Reproduces the metabolite accumulation at the same enzymatic step, by a variant at a residue mutated in human disease.
edges.limitations: A single animal, and its hyperammonaemia is not a reported feature of the human disease, so the presentation is not a match even though the biochemistry is. Beta-aminoisobutyrate was not measured.
edges.source: Feline dihydropyrimidinase deficiency (DPYS p.G435R homozygous cat)

nodes.description: Missense, nonsense, splice-site and deletion variants in DPYS. Most missense variants leave no measurable activity when expressed; structural mapping places them at the tetramer interface, near the di-zinc catalytic centre and substrate site, or in regions where they destabilise folding. Many inactive variants are degraded by the proteasome and fail to form the large oligomers the active enzyme needs.

nodes.description: 5,6-dihydrouracil and 5,6-dihydrothymine accumulate in urine, plasma and cerebrospinal fluid. Beta-aminoisobutyric acid is strongly reduced, while beta-alanine is normal, which distinguishes this block from the upstream DPD deficiency where beta-alanine itself is depleted. Both the symptomatic and the asymptomatic sibling in one family had the same metabolite profile, so the profile alone does not predict whether anyone will be ill.

nodes.description: A naturally occurring case rather than an engineered model: a cat homozygous for a DPYS missense variant at a residue also mutated in a human patient, with dihydrouracil and dihydrothymine in urine. It presented with malnutrition, depression, vomiting and hyperammonaemia. Screening 1,000 cats found no other carrier.

nodes.description: The one actionable intervention in this disease, and it is preventive rather than therapeutic: knowing the diagnosis before a fluoropyrimidine is prescribed. The published argument for it is that severe toxicity has been reported in patients and in carriers of congenital pyrimidine metabolic disorders, so identifying affected people, including the asymptomatic ones, is worthwhile before 5-fluorouracil is given. Note this is a published recommendation rather than a guideline: no dosing algorithm for DPYS exists, unlike DPYD, and the cohort evidence on DPYS variants and toxicity is contested (see the Fluoropyrimidine Cytotoxicity node).

evidence.reference_title: The diagnostic odyssey of a patient with dihydropyrimidinase deficiency: a case report and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Identifying patients with DHP deficiency, even when they are asymptomatic, is warranted to prevent neurotoxicity while administering pyrimidine analog drugs, such as 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), to patients with cancer.

nodes.description: Severe fluoropyrimidine-associated toxicity. In the only cohort that found a signal, carrying at least one rare DPYS variant was associated with about a fourfold higher risk of severe cumulative toxicity; a second cohort genotyping common DPYS variants found no association, so this node is carried as a contested claim and both results are cited.

evidence.reference_title: The burden of rare variants in DPYS gene is a novel predictor of the risk of developing severe fluoropyrimidine-related toxicity.
evidence.snippet: Carrying at least one rare DPYS variant was associated with an approximately fourfold higher risk of severe cumulative (OR = 4.08, P = 0.030) and acute (OR = 4.21, P = 0.082) toxicity.

evidence.reference_title: Common dihydropyrimidinase ( DPYS ) genetic variations do not predict fluoropyrimidine-related chemotherapy toxicity in a Canadian cohort.
evidence.snippet: in our cohort of mostly Caucasian Canadians, genetic variations in DPYS do not appear to be a significant contributor to severe fluoropyrimidine-associated toxicity.

nodes.description: Administration of 5-fluorouracil or a prodrug such as capecitabine. The toxicity arm of this entry is inert without it. It is included because the enzyme that is missing is also the second enzyme of fluoropyrimidine catabolism, and because partial deficiency has been reported as the cause of severe toxicity in a patient.
